notes: Eighteen lists read. oecd.org was not fetched (403 in earlier runs), so OECD entries are the Housing, Safety and Environmental quality indicators as named in the framework key, with one TUAC passage. Eurostat: overcrowding, keep-warm and overburden from Statistics Explained 'Living conditions in Europe - housing' (2024); noise and pollution from the quality-of-life article (2023); the leaking roof/damp/rot figure from Trading Economics' mirror of Eurostat data (2024). Gallup Most Important Problem has no housing row; only Poverty/Hunger/Homelessness and Crime/Violence bear on home. Ipsos has no housing worry; its crime passage is the one country line the page gave. WHO burden lists name household air pollution (open-fire cooking), marked out of scope for U.S. readers. 'High indoor temperatures' is mapped broader to Heating: its alias 'Cold or hot home' suggests heat was meant, but the line names only heating; refine should decide whether to widen it. Living with parents: Pew finds housing costs are not associated with metro rates, so the line avoids naming a cause. Tap water overlaps Pollution (dirty-air) and Infrastructure from the home side. Two drafts (Repairs, Rental applications) come only from the founder pool and have no opened source. Wikidata QIDs from the wbsearchentities API (rate-limited, retried; not counted as searches). PDFs were read locally because the fetch tool could not parse them.
